subject: science
passage: The green of the northern lights comes from oxygen atoms about 100 to 150 kilometers up, which give off green light when fast-moving particles from the sun collide with them. Higher still, where the air is far thinner, oxygen atoms are struck less often and have time to release a deep red light ______ is why the rare all-red auroras appear only at the very top of a display. Nitrogen adds the blue and purple fringes sometimes seen along the lower edge.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Which is why the rare all-red auroras appear only at the very top of a display" is a relative clause that comments on the whole statement before it. Such a clause is not a sentence on its own, so it must be attached to the main clause with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Which is why …" can't stand alone as a sentence, so the period leaves a fragment.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma attaches the "which" clause to the independent clause it explains.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides, but "which is why …" is not one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A "which" clause that comments on the whole preceding statement must be set off with a comma.
